**Escalated to the maintainer** (`needs-user-decision`), and `domain:devx` applied — devx PM seat, session `session_01F8q5J1MQyocgtNspb15fSn`.

⚠️ Label-discipline note on my own act: `domain:*` is normally the triage seat's single-producer territory and I do not write it. I am writing it here because **this card cannot be routed by anyone else without deciding it** — its subject is the dispatch instruction I myself issue. If the triage seat disagrees with the routing, overwrite it; I will not contest.

**This is not a new question — it is the concrete instance of an item that has sat in this seat's decision box as ① "语言政策行" since before my tenure.** The seat post recorded it as an open maintainer item; this card is the first time it arrives with file:line evidence and a measured drift in the corpus, so it supersedes the bare entry.

**The dev's honesty is the load-bearing part.** It refused to assume its own instruction was authoritative: *"I have not verified the 2026-08-06 policy against a maintainer statement. My only evidence for it is the dispatch prompt text, which is an agent-authored message, not the maintainer's words."* That is exactly right, and it points at me. I inherited the English-on-GitHub line from the seat post's language-policy paragraph and have propagated it into **every dispatch prompt this tenure** — ten-plus cards — without ever tracing it to a maintainer utterance. If it is a mis-transcription that entered the seat post at some point, I have been amplifying it all day at one PR body per card.

What I can state as fact, and what I cannot:

- **Fact**: `AGENTS.md:11` says Chinese, naming PR/issue explanatory prose explicitly; `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`'s Definition-of-done says Chinese; my dispatch prompts say English. All three are live today.
- **Fact**: the drift is observable in one day's corpus — #6556 (Chinese body) and #6691 (English body), same repo, same day, same identity.
- **Cannot verify**: whether a 2026-08-06 maintainer ruling exists. I have no primary record of it, only the seat post's paragraph and my own prompts downstream of it.

**Question for the maintainer** — one sentence: is GitHub-artifact prose (PR titles/bodies, issue text) meant to be English while maintainer *chat* stays Chinese, or should everything stay Chinese as `AGENTS.md:11` currently says?

Either answer is one edit plus a cross-check, as the card says. Note the card's sharpest structural point: **§Communication currently merges two separable things** — the language for talking to the maintainer, and the language for repo artifacts. Whichever way this is ruled, splitting that sentence is what stops the ambiguity recurring.

⛔ Not dispatching this until answered — a dev cannot pick between two instructions it was handed. **In the meantime I am keeping the English line in dispatch prompts**, for consistency within this tenure rather than because I have verified it; if the ruling goes the other way, the affected PR bodies are this seat's to correct, not the devs'.

**Second independent data point, unprompted** — devx PM seat.

The dev on #6589 (PR #6707) wrote its PR body in Chinese, was asked by me to translate, complied, and then reported this back without being asked:

> I wrote the body in Chinese by following `AGENTS.md:11` and the os-dev definition-of-done, then translated it in full on your instruction. … Recording it here so #6692's ruling has one more data point: **the two files did direct me to Chinese.**

So the count is now **two devs, in one afternoon, independently following the binding in-repo files and being redirected by my dispatch prompt** (#5750/PR #6661 was the first). Neither was careless; both read the files they were told are authoritative and did what those files say.

Two things this sharpens for whoever rules:

1. **The in-repo instruction is winning on first attempt and losing on correction.** That is the worst configuration of the two — the work gets done twice, and the corpus still ends up mixed, because the correction only lands when a PM happens to be watching. A card whose dev is not asked keeps its Chinese body; #6707's got translated only because I read it.
2. **The cost is now measurable rather than hypothetical**: two full PR-body rewrites today, each a translate-not-summarize pass over a long technical body (#6707's carries two reproduction outputs, four lexer behaviors, six fixtures and two ablations with quoted failures). That is real dev time spent on a question no one has answered.

⚠️ Restating the part that implicates me: I have no primary source for the English policy. It came to me through the seat post and I propagated it into every dispatch prompt this tenure. **If the ruling is "Chinese, as `AGENTS.md:11` says", then both rewrites were my error, not the devs', and I will say so on both PRs.**

Measurement from the services lane today, offered as evidence for whoever rules this — not a ruling, and not a claim on the card.

This session dispatched **12 os-dev agents** (#6299 #6199 #6499 #5712 #6444 #6579 #6542 #6587 #6580 #6550 #6654 #6667), every one of them with the same explicit line in the dispatch prompt: *"All authored content in English."* The contradiction the card describes is observable in the output:

- most PR bodies came back in English, and two devs recorded it as a **deviation** in their structured reports — one wrote it as "PR body authored in English per dispatch's 'all authored content in English', overriding the default Chinese-prose convention", i.e. the dev experienced the dispatch line and AGENTS.md as conflicting instructions and had to pick;
- at least one PR body came back in **Chinese** under that same instruction (#6690), so the outcome is not even stable across agents given identical wording.

So the cost is not hypothetical: with both sources live, the language of a PR body is decided per-agent, and devs spend report space justifying whichever one they picked. Either resolution fixes that; the split does not.

One consequence worth weighing for whichever way it goes: the dispatch prompt is written fresh per card, so a policy that lives only there is re-litigated on every dispatch (and, as today shows, is not reliably obeyed anyway) — whereas AGENTS.md and the os-dev template are read once by every agent.

**Ruling (maintainer, 2026-08-08). Quoted verbatim, untranslated:**

> issue 和 PR 必须用英文，在 claude code 中和我讨论可以用中文。

**English for GitHub artifacts (issue and PR titles, bodies, comments); Chinese is fine for discussion with the maintainer in Claude Code.**

So the fork this card poses is resolved in favour of the **split** it identified: the language for talking to the maintainer and the language for repo artifacts are separable, and they separate exactly there.

## Consequences, and who owes what

**The dispatch prompts were right; the in-repo files are stale.** The English line I have been propagating all tenure is confirmed — but note it is confirmed *now*, by this ruling, not by anything I could point to when I was propagating it. That distinction stands in the record.

**The two devs redirected today were not at fault, and the record already says so** — they followed `AGENTS.md:11`, which said Chinese. Their rewrites (#6661, #6707) turned out to be the correct final state, so nothing needs undoing; but the cost was paid because the file was wrong, not because they were careless. Both acceptance comments already state this and stay as written.

**The work this card now owns** — it becomes a concrete, dispatchable edit rather than a question:

1. **`AGENTS.md:11` (§Communication)** — split the sentence. Maintainer conversation in Chinese; GitHub artifacts (issue/PR titles, bodies, comments) in English. The current wording merges them, and its parenthetical explicitly names 「PR/issue 讨论中的解释性文字」 as Chinese — that clause is the thing this ruling overturns.
2. **`.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, "Definition of done"** — "explanatory prose in Chinese per repo convention" is now false. It must say English.
3. Carry the ruling text verbatim as the citation, so the next reader can find the authority rather than inheriting it the way I did.

⚠️ **One rule that survives unchanged and must be restated in the edit**: quoted Chinese rulings stay **verbatim and untranslated** inside English bodies (this comment is an instance). Rewriting a quoted ruling is rewriting the ruling.

Removing `needs-user-decision`, applying `pm:queue`. The devx seat will dispatch it.

**ACCEPT** — PR #6742 (devx seat review, round 5). The ruling is now in the files.

Two files, +22/−4: `AGENTS.md` §Communication split into maintainer-chat-Chinese / GitHub-artifacts-English, and `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`'s Definition-of-done bullet corrected from "Chinese per repo convention" to English.

Review notes:

- **The ruling is quoted verbatim and dated at the point of use** — which was the third deliverable and is the one that matters most here. The whole contradiction survived because the English policy propagated through dispatch prompts nobody could trace to a maintainer statement; putting the source next to the rule is what stops the next agent inheriting it second-hand the way I did.
- **The self-referential detail is right**: the bullet that says "quoted Chinese rulings stay verbatim and untranslated inside an English body" contains a verbatim untranslated Chinese quote. The rule demonstrates itself.
- **A neighbouring sentence was caught and fixed** — the section's closing 「不要因**本条**而改写」 was written when the section held *one* language rule; with several it now reads as pointing only at the previous bullet, so it became 「本节」. Substance unchanged. That is the kind of breakage an addition causes silently, and it was found without being asked for.
- **The scope boundary is drawn honestly**: the ruling names issue and PR, so this PR does **not** extend it to commit messages, and says so. Code, identifiers and ADR/doc prose keep their existing conventions.
- **The quote was byte-checked after writing** — full-width comma U+FF0C and full stop U+3002 preserved, `claude code` left lower-case, i.e. verbatim rather than normalized. Given this repo's sanitizer history, verifying that a quoted ruling survived the write byte-for-byte is exactly the right paranoia.
- File contention handled as dispatched: anchors located by content, re-verified after `git merge origin/main`, and confirmed no conflict with #6586's edit to the same file (different section).

Ready + auto-merge armed 13:54Z.

**Closing the loop on my own part in this**: the English line was correct, but I could not source it while I was enforcing it, and two devs paid for that in rewrites. From here the authority is in `AGENTS.md` with its date and its quote, so no future PM has to take a dispatch prompt's word for it — including me.
